title: A loop that can light
description: A lamp lights only when the path from the supply and back again is closed. Open that path and the lamp goes dark.

blocks.md:
## A closed path

A lamp lights only when charge can leave the battery, pass through the parts, and return to the battery. That closed path is a series loop. An open gap anywhere on the loop means no current and a dark lamp. Resistance on the loop limits how much current flows.

This bites when you add a lamp but leave a gap, or when you assume “the parts are on the table so it should work.” Being nearby is not a loop. The picture must close.

![A closed series loop](assets/closed-loop.svg)

```text
battery → resistor → lamp → battery
```

A common mistake is thinking an almost-closed path is good enough. The questions ask you to read the pictures — which path can light, and what charge does around a closed loop.

blocks.promptMd: Which diagram is a loop that can light?
blocks.explainMd: Only the closed rectangle lets charge return. The dashed gap is an open path.

blocks.promptMd: Tap the lamp on this closed loop.
blocks.explainMd: The yellow circle at the bottom is the lamp.

blocks.promptMd: Number the path a charge takes around this loop, starting at the battery.
blocks.explainMd: Out of the battery, through the resistor on the right, through the lamp, and home.
